_LANE_TERRITORY_2026-08-06: OWNER-LOCKED PARTITION (Cascade auditor duty, no overlap ever): CC-1 (lane=money) owns ONLY migrations, grants, GL/posting, settlement, WORM, AP/AR, ci.yml DB-env — NEVER routes, NEVER route tests, NEVER rate-limit, NEVER dispatch/mdata scope, NEVER FE. CC-2 (lane=mechanical) owns ONLY routes, route tests, rate-limit, dispatch/mdata entity-scope, FE — NEVER migrations/grants/GL/WORM. Root cause of the 2026-08-06 all-PR-red incident: both builders ran a rate-limit route sweep simultaneously on overlapping route files (a mechanical-lane class assigned to CC-1 in violation of this partition). Before assigning ANY new class, Cascade checks the new card's hotfiles against every OTHER open card's hotfiles; if a money card and a mechanical card share a hotfile, serialize them (one stays queued) instead of running both.

Entity-separation law (docs/IH35-TMS-ARCHITECTURE-AND-BLUEPRINT.md), not cosmetic.

waves.root_cause: Backend code assumes a column or view shape that does not match the live database schema. Postgres resolves column references at PLAN time, so the query 500s on EVERY request, independent of data — not intermittent, not data-dependent. Recurs in two distinct forms: (a) a hand-written SQL query referencing a column a view does not have, and (b) a generic factory/config layer hardcoding a column name/shape that a subset of its target tables do not physically carry.
